findings.title: Tier labels in cases.jsonl name the tier the fixture simulates, not an observation of it; no deterministic case observes the candidate package
criterion_or_requirement: skill-authoring-contract, 'Three separately reported evaluation tiers' (tier C = installed resources AND outputs)
affected_sections: every line: the tier field and candidate_subpath

evidence.description: all 9 cases resolve inside evals/fixtures; none reads the package
--mode installed produces byte-identical results; no case declares a mode, so the file cannot distinguish source from installed
the evaluator-added cases that DO observe the package, demonstrating the graders for this are available and unused

findings.impact: Every case's tier field names the tier its fixture simulates. All 9 set candidate_subpath into evals/fixtures/, so no authored deterministic case observes the package or an installed copy. The four tier:'C' cases cover only the 'outputs' half of the contract's tier C and never the 'templates/references resolve inside the installed package' half; the two tier:'A' cases observe synthetic transcripts, not a session. A reader of a completed run can believe C and A have deterministic coverage when neither does.
findings.uncertainty: Structural inspection is the evaluator's own work under the validator's P2 procedure, and the author's records say tier C 'requires an export or project-local installation that this pass did not perform'. The defect is therefore the labelling and the absent installed-resource half, not a claim that the author owed a full structural suite.

findings.title: Eval case XB-8 declares an old_skill baseline arm that does not exist
criterion_or_requirement: SKILL-004 'Additional common cases': a template placeholder remains in a required result field
skill-authoring-contract, tier B output quality against a baseline

evidence.description: case 8 declares "baseline_comparison": "old_skill"; the other ten cases declare "without_skill"

git -C <candidate-wt> ls-tree -r --name-only c17e758417da64928a0f47fc2600304465ac3f3c providers/claude/plugins/devforgeai/skills/ -> devforge-brainstorm, devforge-develop, devforge-project-expert-creator, devforge-review. states 'No baseline existed' under the Native creator authoring prompt table, contradicting evals.json case 8
line 81 states 'Ten of eleven cases have no old_skill baseline because no prior candidate exists', implying the eleventh does have one

findings.impact: old_skill means a preserved previous revision of the skill; none exists at base c17e758. One of the specification's four required common cases therefore has no runnable comparison arm, and a missing arm supports no improvement claim. The author's stated fallback (authoring-notes.md:107, untrusted: 'that arm is NOT_APPLICABLE with the reason recorded') would additionally misuse the fixed vocabulary, since NOT_APPLICABLE is only for a stated scope exclusion and an absent baseline is not one. The correct arm, without_skill, is available.
findings.uncertainty: none on the fact. The author's rationale (authoring-notes.md:107) is that 'a prior report artifact is the fixture'; that conflates a fixture supplied to a case with a baseline arm of the comparison. Recorded as untrusted explanation, not accepted.

findings.title: SKILL.md overstates what a self-computed plan freeze establishes and routes the correction to a file that does not contain it

evidence.description: "Freeze it - hash the bytes and record the identity - so that a later reader can tell the plan preceded the evidence. [Experiment boundaries](references/experiment-boundaries.md) explains what a freeze does and does not establish here."
"Hashing the plan yourself records which bytes you had; it does not establish that they preceded the evidence to anyone who does not already trust you."
contains no freeze-limit statement; grep for 'preced', 'does not establish', 'self-recorded', 'outside the evaluated' returns no match
the correct operative text: 'self-recorded is self-recorded, and no CLI capability currently binds a plan's bytes outside the evaluated agent's reach'

findings.impact: A material contradiction between the always-loaded entrypoint and the package's own reference, about the exact act the skill says its value depends on (SKILL.md:10, 'The value is entirely in the ordering'). A session that stops at SKILL.md records a self-computed freeze as though it established ordering. Contained because references/recording-rules.md is linked two lines earlier at SKILL.md:48 and gives the field-level instruction correctly.

git -C <validator-wt> diff e52ac59 e641797 --stat -- .../devforge-evaluate-expert/scripts/ -> graders.py and run_cases.py changed, 147 insertions / 16 deletions

findings.impact: The deterministic arm is pinned to a runner revision a bootstrap review found defective and that has since been repaired twice. Not breakage - verified compatible with e641797 - but the recorded dependency identity and its status sentence no longer describe the runner an evaluator would be given.
findings.uncertainty: The correct forward pin depends on which revision of the validator the coordinator will supply to the next evaluation. The change below states the value to record rather than guessing a future one.

findings.title: The --candidate root the authored cases require is recorded nowhere, and the natural wrong value fails silently
affected_sections: runner_dependency (evals.json); the case file as a whole; the fixtures README

evidence.description: --candidate <package root> -> exit 0, complete observations file, all 9 cases COULD_NOT_RUN with cause 'candidate_subpath ... does not resolve to a directory inside the candidate root', zero assertions observed

findings.impact: Passing the package root - the natural reading of 'candidate root' - silently produces a complete observations file at exit 0 with zero assertions observed. That is exactly the silent coverage loss the runner's whole-file rejection design exists to prevent, arriving through the invocation instead of the case file.
findings.uncertainty: The same omission exists in the validator's own package (its cases use the same undocumented convention). That half belongs to the validator's owner and is reported, not fixed here. CHG-005 covers the candidate-side half only.

findings.title: Fixture filenames and the artifact IDs inside them use different numbers
criterion_or_requirement: none - readability of the provenance chain

evidence.description: XPLAN-001.md carries artifact_id "XPLAN-006"; XREPORT-001.md carries "XREPORT-006"; XPLAN-004.md carries "XPLAN-010"; XREPORT-004.md carries "XREPORT-010"
internally consistent: XP-B-001's routed_to correctly cites XPLAN-010@1/XREPORT-010@1, and good/claims/disposition-claim.json correctly cites XPLAN-006@1

findings.impact: A reader matching a case's files list to a routed_to reference has to translate between the filename number and the artifact ID number. No behaviour depends on it and no assertion is affected.
findings.uncertainty: This may be deliberate, to keep fixture filenames stable while the artifact IDs look like realistic project allocations. If so, one sentence in the fixtures README closes it.
